author: Cecilia Levine
title: Netflix Replaces Top Show Boss Behind Your Favorites After Nearly A Decade - NewsBreak
text:
By Cecilia Levine ,
1 hours ago
The woman who oversaw some of Netflix's biggest hits, including "Stranger Things," "Wednesday," and "Squid Game," is leaving the streaming giant after nearly a decade.
Bela Bajaria, Netflix's chief content officer, is departing the company, Netflix announced Thursday, Oct. 15. Peter Rice, a former Disney and Fox executive, will replace her beginning Monday, Oct. 26.
The shakeup comes one day after Netflix co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters told employees on Wednesday, Oct. 14, that the company was cutting about 1,000 jobs, or 6% of its workforce, in its largest round of layoffs yet despite soaring profits.
Bajaria joined Netflix in November 2016 as head of global television before being promoted to chief content officer in January 2023, according to her LinkedIn profile. She oversaw Netflix's global content teams, responsible for hits including "Bridgerton," "Lupin," "Adolescence," "BEEF," "KPop Demon Hunters," and "Frankenstein." Bajaria also led Netflix's expansion into live events and sports, including "The Roast of Tom Brady," Chris Rock's "Selective Outrage," and multiyear deals with the NFL and WWE.
"I want to thank Bela for a decade of dedication, innovation, creativity and leadership," Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos said. "She led enormous changes at Netflix."
Before joining Netflix, Bajaria was president of Universal Television. Her honors include a spot on TIME's 100 Most Influential People list in 2022 and recognition among Fortune's Most Powerful Women for eight years.
Rice previously served as chairman of Walt Disney Television and chairman of general entertainment for Disney, overseeing programming across ABC, Hulu, FX, National Geographic, and other networks. At Netflix, he will oversee scripted and unscripted series, films, live events, and other programming worldwide.
Programs under his leadership included "The Bear," "Abbott Elementary," "Modern Family," "This Is Us," and "Only Murders in the Building." He also previously led Fox Searchlight Pictures, which released films including "Slumdog Millionaire," "Juno," and "Little Miss Sunshine."
"I'm grateful to Bela for building such a remarkable global team, and I look forward to building on everything she and the team have created," Rice said.
